dish: Wheeling-style square cheese pizza — cold hand-grated aged provolone piled on a crisp square crust after it leaves the oven
w: The original Wheeling home of Ohio Valley-style pizza: the DiCarlo brothers opened here in 1949 and the cold-cheese-on-hot-crust method became a regional icon.

dish: Fried fish sandwich — a cluster of hot fried filets between two slices of soft white bread
w: A Centre Market institution since 1914 turning out 1,000+ fish sandwiches a day (2,500 on Fridays); called the country's best fish sandwich by Gourmet and featured on Food Network.

dish: Spaghetti with Anna Figaretti's homemade Sicilian sauce
address: 1035 Mount de Chantal Rd, Wheeling, WV 26003
w: A 2026 James Beard America's Classics winner; family-run since 1948 from Anna Figaretti's garage-made sauce, and previously named the best Italian restaurant in West Virginia.

dish: Elevated Appalachian New American plates from chef Matt Welsch (a WV Chef Ambassador and Food Network winner)
w: Downtown gastropub from chef Matt Welsch — one of WV's inaugural Chef Ambassadors and a Food Network competition winner — serving locally sourced New American takes on Appalachian comfort food.

dish: Savory and sweet crepes
w: A cornerstone of Center Wheeling's revival since 2006, set in an 1860 building that won a $50,000 National Trust Backing Historic Small Restaurants grant; known for its wide crepe menu.

dish: Croissants, quiche and the 'almost famous' Salty Bread
w: Chef Sarah Lydick's downtown bakery-cafe (opened 2018 in the former Lebanon Bakery) that won the Show of Hands pitch contest and quickly became one of Wheeling's most beloved spots.

dish: Award-winning burgers and fresh-cut fries
w: Locally sourced American fare in the restored Waterfront Hall on the Wheeling riverfront, known for its burgers, fries and a menu that shifts with the seasons.

dish: GrecoRoni pepperoni rolls, served with marinara or the house dressing
w: A longtime Wheeling neighborhood Italian spot whose 'world famous' GrecoRoni pepperoni rolls are a local tradition — Weelunk's pick in the best-pepperoni-roll conversation.

dish: Tavern fare and pizza at the reborn Alpha (the former Ye Olde Alpha, a nearly 90-year Wheeling landmark)
n: The Alpha Tavern (formerly Ye Olde Alpha)
w: The Edgwood site that was Ye Olde Alpha for nearly 90 years (est. 1932); after the old building came down it was rebuilt and revived by the Sparachanes as The Alpha Tavern in 2020.

dish: Ohio Valley craft beer and brewpub fare (CLOSED)
w: Centre Market brewpub founded 2014 that helped resurrect Wheeling's brewing heritage and anchor downtown revival; now permanently closed but a notable chapter of the district's comeback.

dish: The 'everything' hot dog — a frank with mustard, onions and Shorty's homemade chili sauce
w: A Washington, PA hot-dog lunch counter since the early 1930s, run by the Alexas family; its chili-topped 'everything' dog commands the kind of loyalty most brands only dream of.

dish: Real Italian spaghetti and fresh Italian bread
w: Founded 1939 as the West Chestnut Spaghetti Inn by Palermo immigrants Angelo and Giacomina Passalacqua, it grew into Washington's most beloved Italian institution — 8+ decades and still family-run.

dish: Seasonal local menu in an 1794 National Road stagecoach inn (the Keeping Room's original kitchen fireplace still stands)
address: 2175 E National Pike (US-40), Scenery Hill, PA 15360
w: Built 1794 as Hill's Tavern, the oldest continuously operating inn on the National Road; on the National Register, it sheltered Presidents Washington, Jackson and Polk and reopened after a 2015 fire.

dish: Italian-American fine dining with Mediterranean touches (salmon, pollo caprese, stuffed steak)
w: Opened 1967 and named for the stonemasons and union workers who filled its tavern; a downtown Washington fixture for Italian-American cooking and an Observer-Reporter Best-of-the-Best regular.

dish: Handmade chocolates and old-fashioned ice-cream-parlour sundaes beside a 1,500-lb chocolate castle
w: Frank Sarris started making chocolate in his Canonsburg basement in 1960; the block-long factory store and Ice Cream Parlour is a Washington County landmark that draws visitors from across the region.

dish: Scratch-made cafeteria classics on a rotating steam line (a Route 40 tradition since 1961)
address: 51800 National Rd E, St. Clairsville, OH 43950
w: A fourth-generation Ohio Valley staple on the National Road since 1961, serving Mary Mehlman's scratch-made favorites; WTRF and others have called it among the best cafeterias in Ohio.

dish: Gourmet Italian dishes and steak specials overlooking the Ohio Valley
w: The St. Clairsville outpost of the Undo's family (original in Benwood, WV, since 1953), a Belmont County local favorite for Italian cooking with a valley view and a sports bar.

dish: The Gulla Dog — a hot dog under the family's red, spicy Sicilian chili sauce, onions and mustard
w: An 85-year Bellaire hot-dog institution now in its fourth Gulla generation, built on a great-grandmother's Sicilian chili-sauce recipe brought over from the old country.

dish: Coney Island coney dogs and Mile-High Meringue pie
w: Downtown Cambridge on the National Road since 1931 (as Coney Island Lunch), family-run by the Theodosopoulos family since 1963; its coney dogs have been a mainstay for over 90 years.

dish: Chinese tea (thumbprint) cookies, shipped worldwide, plus devil-dog pastries and glazed donuts
w: A from-scratch Cambridge bakery running on the same family recipes since 1925; its Chinese tea cookies are so beloved that fans have them shipped as far as Germany.

dish: The Tin Roof Sundae, served in a soup bowl
w: A Zanesville institution since 1948, named after a customer who demanded his sundae be served in a soup bowl; a USA Today-recognized ice-cream stop known for its Tin Roof sundaes.

dish: Hand-made pastas and daily-made pizza dough in a Tuscan-style dining room
w: On Zanesville's Maple Avenue since 1958 and still family-run; Pizza Today has ranked it among the top 100 independently owned pizzerias in the nation.

dish: Award-winning Anastasia Russian Imperial Stout and scratch-made brewpub pizza
w: The first brewery to operate in Zanesville since Prohibition (opened 2007 by Jay and Lori Wince) in a riverside brick building; an Ohio Magazine-featured craft brewpub known for its imperial stout.

dish: House-made pasta, pizza and steaks (CLOSED — reopening as Market Street Prime)
w: A downtown Zanesville steak-and-Italian mainstay for 51 years; it closed in May 2025 and the Market Street space is being reborn under new ownership as the upscale Market Street Prime.
